Choose page internals for the actual work; adapt the starter rather than imposing every section. Keep facts, evidence and approval boundaries honest. Verify the native saved result and tell me what remains unverified.

<content>
**Edition 1 · <mention-date start="2026-10-11"/>**
Portable instructions for any collaborating AI with the relevant capabilities. Give it this full page or the text download, then the project-specific inputs.
<file src="notion-file-block://089c177a-0b4c-46e3-870c-71115dfeda1e/0d11c87a-c97a-47ea-a3d4-c23fe0c834fb?space_id=1973bdb6-edb1-4c28-9480-b7a6ac2f9a4c&name=Notion-Hub-AI-Brief.txt">Download the complete AI brief (.txt)</file>
<details>
<summary>Contents</summary>
	<table_of_contents/>
</details>
Use this skill when Ahmed asks to create, adapt or tidy a Notion project hub in his established style. When Ahmed says “cards” in this hub workflow, he means native Board/Kanban cards grouped into columns, unless he explicitly asks for a gallery. Do not substitute a Gallery view for that request.
The outcome is a usable native workspace that makes purpose, current position and next action obvious, with deeper work easy to reach. This is for hub structure and evidence-backed organization; it does not authorize executing the project, sharing data, or rebuilding unrelated systems.
## Inputs for this run
- Project and outcome: what is this hub for?
- Operation: new hub, adapt a starter, or refine an existing hub?
- Sources: exact existing pages, databases, files and current user direction.
- Destination: exact target, or a new private standalone page.
- Known state and next action: include evidence dates and any uncertainty.
- Domain and useful working lens: phases, versions, opportunity stage, reading mode, categories or another justified choice.
- Boundaries: what must be preserved, what is out of scope, and any approval gates.
Infer reversible layout choices from the sources. Ask only for a missing fact or decision that materially changes the result. If the project state is unknown, create an honest orientation shell and mark it unknown rather than inventing progress.
## 1. Inspect before creating
Search for the project, its existing hub, Registry entry, reusable templates and canonical data source. Read the target and relevant child pages, including representative nested working pages and database-record bodies. Inspect their internal structure, not only the home. Inspect actual schemas, saved view configurations, record counts, representative cards and native navigation. Do not infer the architecture from the page title or a text summary.
Read the current user direction alongside dated project evidence. A recent page edit is not proof that every status inside is current. Separate observed or measured results, user reports, proposals, historical checkpoints and unknowns. Resolve consequential conflicts or state them.
Use the existing system when it already fits. Do not create a parallel database for the same items, duplicate a portfolio/reading system, or rebuild an established hub simply to apply a style.
## 2. Choose the smallest useful architecture
Use four layers when needed:
- Home: purpose, current state, one concrete next action and deliberate navigation.
- Work surfaces: one canonical source per genuine entity type, with each database on its own child page and genuine saved views.
- Working rooms: active notes, planning, evidence/results and a latest handoff where useful.
- Reference/history: definitions, background and dated checkpoints, separate or collapsed.
These are roles, not mandatory page counts. Combine small rooms or omit unused ones. A light project may need only a home, one database and notes. A substantial project can keep several purpose-built rooms.
The project hub should remain a standalone home. A Projects & Ideas Registry record can point to it through the existing Key Link/Home or equivalent properties. The Registry classifies and reminds; it is not the container for the complete project workspace. For an existing nested hub, inspect permissions and get direction before moving it. Linking is the safer fallback when inherited access cannot be verified.
## 3. Build the home for a quick return
Start with one sentence of purpose. Put the main working entry near the top, then a short current checkpoint and next action/decision. Use source dates where they matter. Keep the first screen useful; avoid repeating the whole roadmap or dumping database fields onto it.
Prefer an explicit saved-view link for the main entry. For a phase-driven project, a board can be the best first stop for seeing what is current, next and exploratory. A gallery is an optional alternate for browsing experiments, resources or distinct capabilities. Board/Kanban is the primary interpretation of his card-based working surface. Choose its grouping by the user's question and latest preference, not a universal gallery-first rule. Keep the alternate gallery and full table available.
Keep active navigation visible. Use short room names and a one-line explanation only when needed. Put dense methodology, long dictionaries, old checklists and superseded rationale in child pages or real native toggles. Never hide the only route to active work inside history.
A compact home scaffold:
Purpose: one sentence.
Open the working board/gallery: exact saved-view link.
Current position: real state, evidence date and current focus.
Next action or decision: one concrete move and any gate.
Working rooms: notes/handoff, evidence/decisions, reference/history as needed.
Portfolio tracking: the existing Registry entry, if applicable.
## 4. Adapt the records and views
One item exists once in the canonical source for its entity type. Views are attention filters over that source; they are not separate copies. Distinct entities may need separate databases: finance setup tasks, recurring obligations and actual payment transactions are different things. Create only the entity structures the requested work needs.
Start with only useful fields: title, actual status, a short purpose/outcome, next action, source and evidence date. Add a grouping field and area/type when they improve navigation. Keep evidence basis when reported, measured, planned and unknown states could otherwise be confused. Use hidden display Order only when it helps.
Keep concepts separate:
- Phase/version/category = where it belongs.
- Status/lifecycle = what is true now.
- Priority = what deserves attention.
- Area/type = what kind of thing it is.
- Evidence basis/freshness = how it is known and how current the evidence is.
Do not turn a critical idea into completed work, a phase into proof of progress, or a colorful label into a percentage.
Saved views should answer distinct questions:
- Board: sequence or grouping at a glance. Group by the relevant field.
- Gallery: browse recognizable cards. Show title/icon and a few decision-useful properties, usually status, area, concise result and next step.
- Current/next table: narrow operational queue with explicit filters.
- All items/full data: genuinely unfiltered source index, including completed, stale and archived-category records. Hiding a row from a working view never deletes it.
Add a calendar only for real dates, a timeline only for meaningful ranges, and a chart only for an actual quantitative question. Do not copy every view from the examples.
Use an owned child database for a duplicable starter, not a linked view into a live project. After duplication, confirm the new data-source identity, child links and view IDs before changing records; a copied mention or view-specific URL may still point to the master. Repoint them deliberately. Do not promise automatic remapping or a universal default tab.
## 5. Use the visual language purposefully
Use native Notion blocks, a relevant page icon, clear section hierarchy, restrained colored callouts and readable spacing. Avoid putting the same emoji in both icon and title. A cover is optional and should serve recognition; the inspected control centers work without one.
Blue can orient, green can mark a confirmed principle or completed outcome, amber can signal a pending decision, and gray can hold background. Keep each field's colors internally consistent. Text labels must carry the meaning without color. Red Area does not automatically mean failure. Exact colors are adaptable conventions, not a universal status code.
Use columns for a short comparison or navigation grouping when they remain readable on smaller screens. Avoid decorative density, many empty sections, wide five-column layouts copied without a reason, and prose pretending to be cards. Cards must be real native board/gallery records.
Choose the body by the page's job:
- A planning page leads with current direction and boundaries, then ordered tracks, evidence gaps and decisions, with dated rationale kept separately.
- A substantial board card leads with its real lifecycle, then why it matters, intended/observed outcome, next gate and governing source.
- A working or drafting page opens directly onto the work. Put requirements/reference in a neighboring page; keep the best current assembled output separate from raw iteration when that helps.
- An evidence report leads with the finding and conditions, keeps its charts/results visibly accessible, and collapses long methodology/reconciliation.
- A handoff leads with the current stopping point, important changes, source route and exact resumption step.
- A lightweight registry/reading record can have no body when properties already carry purpose, source, resume position and next step. Do not add empty template bureaucracy.
Keep long measured results with the canonical evidence page. Use the supplied source map to choose the closest real pattern.
## 6. Preserve facts, access and history
Do not overwrite sources, change sharing, move live pages or delete meaningful records just to simplify the home. Read before editing; make the smallest complete change. Preserve child page/database blocks, IDs, links, attachments, formulas, relations and rich-text mentions.
Use native references when linking existing Notion pages. Be careful: a child-page or database block can move the referenced object; a mention is only a link. Preserve unrelated content and inspect permissions before a hierarchy change. If access is unclear, leave the source where it is and link it.
Keep dated history and clearly say what supersedes it. Never manufacture versions, milestones, completion, measurements, review dates, sources or permission. A planning page is not approval to execute. Future financial-system examples are architecture suggestions only; do not create balances, transactions, account records or import financial data without a concrete authorized request.
## 7. Verify the saved workspace
Before reporting success:
- Fetch the saved home, rooms, database, representative records and every created or changed view.
- Confirm expected parents, native block types and working navigation.
- Confirm schemas, grouping, displayed fields, sorts and exact filters.
- Query saved views to check membership/counts and ensure views of the same entity share its canonical source.
- Confirm the full-data view is unfiltered. Do not relabel an existing filtered Default view as All.
- Verify key claims against sources; preserve unknown and historical labels.
- Check no live evidence was lost, moved, duplicated or exposed.
- If browser access is available, open the home and primary view, inspect card readability and narrow-screen navigation. State which visual checks actually happened.
A successful write or native configuration readback is not a screenshot review. If visual access is blocked, say that native structure was verified and rendered appearance remains unreviewed.
Return the hub and primary-view links, a short explanation of the adaptation and any real limitation. Do not claim installation, publication, enablement or duplication testing that did not occur.
## Missing inputs and tools
If another AI cannot read private Notion links, ask for exported/pasted source content and this brief. If it cannot create or inspect native views, provide a clearly labeled build specification or ready-to-paste draft and identify that native setup remains. Do not present formatted text as a saved gallery or a local file as an installed skill.
For a new hub with no named destination, use a private standalone draft when supported. Preserve existing sharing. For a requested existing target, inspect and adapt it in place within scope.
## Reuse and maintenance
Keep the method stable; refresh project facts every run. Treat names, dates, examples, phases, versions and field options as inputs. Update the canonical playbook and this brief when Ahmed asks for a lasting hub-design change. Do not turn an incidental project choice into a universal requirement.
Canonical guide: <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f6bd7ade63b81d08510fc4032676f74">My Notion Hub Playbook</mention-page>
Practical starter: <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f6bd7ade63b81b1b255ed27c85c8bec"/>
Domain adaptations and inspected sources: <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f6bd7ade63b81e98048c4618ba613b0"/>
This page is a native Notion Skill and portable AI brief. It is not a Codex skill installed on a computer, and a private link alone does not guarantee another AI can read it.
</content>
</page>

</callout>
## Choose the page by the job
The common formula is **orient → choose → work → verify → resume**. The inside of each page changes with its purpose. Do not create every recipe below for every project.
### Working home
**Use for:** a project’s daily return point.
**Scaffold:** one-sentence purpose → top board entry → current state/evidence date → next action/decision → visible working-room links → quiet history/reference route.
**Keep out:** long field dictionaries, complete research transcripts and repeated copies of database records.
### Planning or roadmap page
**Use for:** decisions, scope and sequence before execution.
**Scaffold:** purpose → current baseline and maturity → current direction/ordered sequence → work tracks → evidence gaps → decisions/approval gates → dated earlier rationale.
**Keep distinct:** chosen scope, proposed outcomes, observed results and superseded plans. Version names are appropriate only when the project really has versions.
### Substantial board-card page
**Use for:** a feature, experiment or work item that needs more than its properties.
**Scaffold:** status/basis callout → why it matters → intended or observed result → relevant scope/conditions → next gate/action → governing source.
**Keep small:** the card summarizes and points to the detailed source. A plan card must not become a second competing plan.
### Drafting or production room
**Use for:** writing or building a concrete output.
**Scaffold:** current working section first → raw contribution / refinement as useful → best current assembled output → compact review checklist.
**Neighbors when useful:** requirements/reference, optional proof or large tests. Create them only when they reduce friction. Preserve the submitted/final version separately from later practice.
### Evidence or research report
**Use for:** substantial findings or measurements.
**Scaffold:** question and finding → conditions/date → visible results and short interpretation → supported conclusion → limitations → collapsible source/method/reconciliation detail → usable downloads when appropriate.
**Preserve:** measured versus reported facts, exact conditions and accessible charts. Compact navigation should not hide the deliverable itself.
### Handoff or living reference
**Handoff scaffold:** latest checkpoint → what actually changed → stopping point → source route → exact next action and blockers.
**Deep-guide scaffold:** purpose/audience → short overview → progressively deeper explanations → responsibility map → question-based reading routes → source map and current maturity.
**History scaffold:** dated context → observation/result → lesson → current implication → sources and what not to copy blindly.
### Lightweight registry or reading card
**Use for:** selection, tracking and resumption.
**Scaffold:** useful properties may be enough: identity/source, why it matters, status, load, resume position and next step. A blank body is legitimate when the real knowledge lives elsewhere.
**Do not add:** mandatory empty headings, invented percentages or copied source documents merely for uniformity.
## 1 · The Freelancing Arc
**Home:** <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3e0bd7ade63b81789097d1e1181cccb9"/>.
**Work surface:** <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/00be3c9d984b44d9a4055070be3b3007"/>.

The native Fit Map board groups by Fit; the full table and specialized tables/boards use the same records. Working-view freshness filters preserve old records while reducing current noise.
**Transfer:** keep factual status, present attention and evidence freshness separate. “Saved” does not mean “committed.” Use a short operational surface over durable detail.
**Do not copy blindly:** job-specific Fit, Connects, Time Fit or Freshness gates into unrelated projects.
<details>

	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f3bd7ade63b8123afe6fba48c4151b3"/> — current stopping point first, contribution history, calibrated lessons, operational state, authoritative reading route and exact resumption sequence.
</details>
## 2 · FFmpeg Encoder
**Home:** <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f2bd7ade63b8137a25ccedb3c87c381"/>.
**Native board:** [Features by version](https://app.notion.com/p/60570a27dd79480f9e567e0dd8db6d8e?v=3f2bd7ade63b81fa9cbf000cdc3ec91d).

<details>
<summary>Nested sources and their internal design</summary>
	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3e5bd7ade63b81d5a7fcd46a0a753aae"/> — purpose and planning-only callouts, overview/sequence, technical tracks, evidence gaps, decisions/handoff and preserved historical rationale. Current direction explicitly supersedes older assumptions.
	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f2bd7ade63b8183a7cbc555e8ad100b"/> — a real feature card: lifecycle callout, why it matters, proposed outcome, next decision/gate and source of truth.
	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f2bd7ade63b8182a322e89b5a6e0498"/> — compact board-reading instructions, collapsible semantic tag legend and explicit source/approval roles.
</details>
## 3 · Local AI
**Home:** <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3d2bd7ade63b8198ba77ed1578dc3b22"/>.
**Native board:** [Experiments by phase](https://app.notion.com/p/89be7e19d97d4397acc814340f1a5b21?v=3f6bd7ade63b814a89ba000cc08574b8).
**Observed:** a standalone project home with current focus, measured results and working ideas separated from earlier history. Seven experiment records share a phase board, optional gallery, evidence table and current/next table. The latest requested entry is near the top and explicitly opens the phase board; a view-specific link is distinct from changing global tab order.
**Transfer:** use phases and evidence-aware status wording for R&D. Reported completion, measured records, running-but-unconfirmed work, planned setup and discussion remain distinguishable.
**Do not copy blindly:** model names, hardware, test settings or software versions into another project.
<details>
<summary>Nested sources and their internal design</summary>
	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3eebd7ade63b81e4a4bcec55419a4a88"/> — dated working notes that separate observations, hypotheses, measured evidence, proposed pilots and open questions.
	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3d9bd7ade63b81f281badac7565369e5"/> — purpose, stage sequence, desired outcomes, boundaries and exit conditions; its earlier “now” statements are historical, not a current status authority.
	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f6bd7ade63b8178b3dbd7e7174ced9e"/> — pilot card with explicit candidate state, purpose, intended result, restricted scope, next gate and evidence.
	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f4bd7ade63b81d99140e0000839431b"/> — evidence report with a finding-first opening, setup, seven visible charts, short interpretations, collapsed methodology/source-reconciliation sections and three downloads. This inspection checks structure; it does not repeat its measurement audit.
</details>
## 4 · Projects & Ideas Control Center
**Home:** <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3d2bd7ade63b818f9b81ec3076427097"/>.
**Registry:** <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/d8eb25dc9ada4e59987c86feff5504e1"/>.
**Existing reusable portfolio template:** <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3d2bd7ade63b8116bd03d65cc0d3abd0"/>.
**Observed:** purpose → Capture/Classify/Focus → core principle → layers/field primer → collapsible dictionaries → view guide/operating rhythm. Native Registry views include a status board, focused tables and a cognitive-load chart. There is no gallery in this inspected center. Its Default table is filtered to current statuses and must not be mistaken for an all-records view.
**Transfer:** priority, status, load, human attention and next action answer different questions. The Registry is portfolio memory; a dedicated hub holds detailed work.
**Do not duplicate:** the existing portfolio template already supplies a whole portfolio system. This new starter fills the separate need for an individual project home.
<details>
<summary>Nested sources, including a legacy exception</summary>
	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3d3bd7ade63b8136b672d39aba46d790"/> — deep whiteboard reference: purpose/audience, overview table, grammar and examples, workflows, edge cases, compact reference, present state and preservation rules.
	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3d2bd7ade63b8193b23bf01c5b00531d"/> — PBS is an existing Registry entry whose body acts as a hub with three true children. This is an observed legacy exception, not permission to keep nesting new hubs.
	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3dcbd7ade63b814a839be43790f8c390"/> — Human Guide: 90-second overview, progressive explanation, question-based file atlas, reading paths, beginner/expert summaries, document-creation triggers and source map.
	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3dabd7ade63b81f489fcedf166bf7c5e"/> — experimental architecture: maturity → target → responsibilities → operating and recovery boundaries → evidence/uncertainty.
	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3dabd7ade63b81fda0edd1861828d882"/> — evolutionary evidence log: generations, successes/failures, lessons, implications and what not to copy.
	**Evidence caution:** older PBS pages and the newer Human Guide disagree about the migration’s recorded completion. No live status is reconciled or rewritten by this template work.
</details>
## 5 · Reading & Knowledge Control Center
**Home:** <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3d7bd7ade63b81f49de0faa2047cb793"/>.
**Registry:** <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/e8a8c4d6dcb34ba09e0a40c494440015"/>.
**Existing reusable reading template:** <mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3d7bd7ade63b80c18587cde1aecb6b27"/>.
**Observed:** purpose → Capture/Classify/Resume → field primer → collapsible dictionaries → question-based view guide and operating rhythm. Native reading pipeline board, Resume Here and other tables; no inspected gallery. Resume From and Next Reading Step are central. Progress percentage is optional.
**Transfer:** organize for easy continuation. A source can remain reference material without becoming a project. Preserve the difference between paused, stalled, reference, archived and deliberately dropped.
**Do not copy blindly:** software versions or delivery milestones. Do not duplicate the already-existing reading-system template.
<details>
<summary>Nested records: useful without page bodies</summary>
	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3dcbd7ade63b81aabe16da7e1a00d07c"/> — PBS Human Guide reading card.
	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3e0bd7ade63b8172a037c81e7b5b247e"/> — Raising Conscious Sons.
	<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3e0bd7ade63b811db6a9dbaf7888d082"/> — human history/time/relativity thread.
	All three inspected records have blank bodies. Their identity, purpose, source, load, resume position, next step and notes are in properties. The PBS reading card links to the deep guide instead of duplicating it. This is a valid finished structure, not an incomplete template.
</details>
## Future adaptation · Personal Financial System
This is an architectural example only, not a created finance hub or financial record.
- Home: purpose, date/period, what needs attention and one next decision.
- Work surface: a board of setup work, reviews or system components if those are the entities being managed.
- Separate data structures only when they represent genuinely different things, such as recurring obligations versus recorded transactions. Do not force unlike records into one generic task list.
- Evidence room: definitions, source/period and reconciliation notes, with explicit unknowns.
- Reference: policies, historical decisions and archived periods.
Use only the financial information and exact destination Ahmed authorizes. Do not invent balances, account details, budgets or transactions; do not import sensitive records merely to demonstrate a template.
## Why the chart playbook matters
<mention-page url="https://app.notion.com/p/3f4bd7ade63b817ea5b9e280616c81ab"/> supplies the packaging pattern: stable method, variable inputs, a complete portable AI brief, real examples, explicit evidence boundaries and an acceptance checklist. This hub playbook uses that repeatability without copying chart-only typography, hardware strips or branding.
## What was preserved
This task created a separate private resource. It did not rewrite, move or share the inspected hubs, registries, working pages or evidence. The starter contains only three explicitly labeled demonstration cards and no real project/financial records. Its native views share one owned data source.
</content>
</page>

For unsubmitted opportunities, the currentness gate is: **active pre-application Stage + Priority is not Pass + Freshness is 🟢 Recent signal or 🟡 Recheck needed**. These are views of the same underlying records: - **🚦 Fit Map — primary visual work surface.** Grouped by Strong / Conditional / Poor Fit, but filtered to the **current actionable/recheckable market plus real active applications**. This is the default board for visually auditing opportunities. A historical Strong Fit does not stay here merely because it once matched. - **🌱 Current Review — Start Here** — compact table using the same currentness gate for **pre-application** candidates only. Best when you want a smaller inspection list rather than the board layout. - **🕰️ Freshness Map** — shows how records aged: Recent signal, Recheck needed, Stale evidence, Inactive \>14d, or Retired / historical. Use it to audit old research and why something left the live queue. - **📋 All Opportunities** — complete source-of-truth table. Historical, stale, skipped and retired records remain here; hiding a row from a working view never deletes or rewrites it. - **🎯 Apply Next / Priority views** — narrower action views when a job has already earned higher attention. - **🌙 Schedule Map** — current pre-application jobs grouped by Cairo schedule impact, using the same freshness boundary. - **🔐 Logged-in Check** — current pre-application jobs where Ahmed still needs private Upwork-only verification, using the same freshness boundary. - **🗃️ Proposal History / Outcomes** — submitted and finished applications. > **View rule:** the database is memory; the working views are attention filters. **Fit describes the job. Freshness helps decide whether it deserves present visibility. Stage records our relationship with it. Priority says what we should do next.** ## 🏷️ Classification dictionary {toggle="true"} ## 🏷️ Terminology dictionary — what every main tag means **The core classification questions are:** **Stage = Where is it in our relationship with the job?** · **Fit = How well does the work itself match?** · **Priority = What should we do next?** · **Freshness = How current is the evidence / should it stay in live views?** · **Client Risk = How safe/credible is the client?** · **Tool Gap = How much missing expertise is there?** · **Time Fit = What does the schedule mean in Cairo?** ## 🚦 Stage — *Where is this opportunity in our workflow?* {toggle="true"}
Stage Meaning
🔎 **Scouted** Found and recorded. Interesting enough to preserve, but not yet promoted.
⭐ **Shortlist** Strong enough to deserve deliberate inspection.
🔐 **Logged-in Check** Ahmed needs to open the private Upwork page for hidden/account-specific details before we decide.
✍️ **Preparing** We have decided to apply and are tailoring the proposal/test/video.
📤 **Submitted** Proposal has been sent.
👀 **Viewed** Confirmed client view, when Upwork exposes that signal.
💬 **Interview** Client has opened active conversation/interview.
📨 **Offer** A formal offer exists but has not yet become a contract.
✅ **Hired** Contract accepted / client relationship began.
📭 **No Response** Enough time passed without reply that we administratively close it as silence — not as proven rejection.
❌ **Rejected** Explicit rejection or clear negative outcome.
🗃️ **Closed** Opportunity closed for another known reason.
⏭️ **Skipped** We deliberately chose not to spend a proposal on it.
## 🧩 Fit — *How well does the actual role match Ahmed?* {toggle="true"}
Fit Meaning
🟢 **Strong Fit** Core responsibilities map directly to existing support experience, portfolio proof, communication strengths, and realistic learnability.
🟡 **Conditional Fit** Viable, but there is a meaningful stretch: schedule, phone work, SaaS context, tool gap, mixed VA duties, or another condition we must consciously accept.
🔴 **Poor Fit** Major mismatch in expertise, scope, communication channel, schedule, economics, or job nature.
> **Fit is intentionally historical as well as current.** If a job was genuinely a Strong Fit when inspected, later staleness does not require us to falsify that assessment. **Freshness + Stage + Priority decide whether it remains in the live Fit Map.** ## 🎯 Priority — *What should happen next?* {toggle="true"}
Priority Meaning
🥇 **Apply Next** Best current candidate. Verify remaining details and move toward proposal unless a new blocker appears.
🥈 **Strong Review** Promising enough to inspect seriously, but another candidate currently deserves attention first.
👁️ **Watch** Worth preserving, but not strong enough to spend immediate attention/Connects.
⏭️ **Pass** Do not spend more active attention unless new information materially changes the case.
## 🕰️ Freshness — *How current is the evidence, and does this belong in the live queue?* {toggle="true"}
Freshness Meaning
🟢 **Recent signal** We have reasonably recent dated evidence that makes the opportunity worth keeping in the live review surface. This does **not** guarantee the listing is still accepting applications.
🟡 **Recheck needed** The opportunity is recent/relevant enough to preserve in the live queue, but an important current fact still needs verification before Connects are spent.
🕰️ **Stale evidence** Our available evidence is too old or weak for the job to occupy the live pre-application views. Stale evidence alone does **not** prove the client has been continuously inactive.
💤 **Inactive \>14d** A dated source explicitly reported more than two weeks of client inactivity at that snapshot. This is stronger than ordinary staleness, but it still describes the evidence date rather than proving the client never returned later.
⏭️ **Retired / historical** We deliberately removed the opportunity from present application attention, or it now exists only as historical/learning material. Historical Fit and reasoning are preserved.
**Live-view rule for unsubmitted jobs:** Stage must still be a pre-application working stage, Priority must not be Pass, and Freshness must be **Recent signal** or **Recheck needed**. **Submitted / Viewed / Interview / Offer** are treated separately and remain visible as active relationships even if public listing evidence ages. > **Example:** Pokémon can remain historically **🟢 Strong Fit** while being **⏭️ Skipped · ⏭️ Pass · ⏭️ Retired / historical** and therefore absent from the live Fit Map. ## ⚠️ Client Risk — *How comfortable are we with the client?* {toggle="true"}
Risk Meaning
🟢 **Low Risk** Hiring/spend/history/payment signals look reasonably healthy and no major concern is visible.
🟡 **Medium Risk** Some concern or uncertainty deserves clarification: limited history, scope ambiguity, odd feedback, extreme availability wording, etc.
🔴 **High Risk** Material warning signs make the opportunity unsafe or strategically weak unless resolved.
⚪ **Unknown** Not enough evidence yet.
> **Fit and Client Risk are deliberately separate.** Proposal #1 was a strong role fit but carried meaningful client-side uncertainty. ## 🛠️ Tool Gap — *How much missing platform/tool knowledge exists?* {toggle="true"}
Tool Gap Meaning
🟢 **Low Gap** Tools are already familiar, simple enough, or not central to selection.
🟡 **Learnable** Some missing Shopify/Gorgias/Zendesk/Intercom/etc. familiarity, but the role does not demand deep pre-existing mastery.
🔴 **Significant** The job clearly depends on expertise Ahmed does not currently have.
⚪ **Unknown** Not enough detail yet.
## 🌙 Time Fit — *What does the schedule mean in Cairo?* {toggle="true"}
Time Fit Meaning
🟢 **Cairo-Friendly** Known schedule sits mainly inside a normal Cairo daytime/evening pattern.
🟡 **Late / Split** Requires late-evening availability, split check-ins, or a timezone window that may extend into night. Needs deliberate inspection before applying.
🔴 **Night-Heavy** Known or strongly constrained schedule runs materially into Cairo overnight hours and would require a serious tradeoff to justify.
⚪ **Unknown** The listing does not give enough schedule information. Client city alone is never used to invent a shift.
**🕒 Schedule Clarity** tells us whether the listing gives an exact clock range, only a timezone/business-hours window, or nothing usable. **🇪🇬 Cairo-Time Reference** stores the translated local meaning and any ambiguity. > **September 19, 2026 reference:** Cairo is UTC+3. It is currently +7h vs US Eastern, +8h vs Central, +9h vs Mountain, +10h vs Pacific, and 1 hour behind Gulf/GCC time. Daylight-saving transition dates differ, so long-term contracts should be rechecked when clocks change. ## 🧾 Supporting tags — *fast context at a glance* {toggle="true"}
Field Examples / meaning
💳 **Contract** ⏱️ Hourly · 📦 Fixed-price
📨 **Channels** ✉️ Email · 💬 Chat · ☎️ Phone · 🟢 WhatsApp · 📱 Social
🧾 **Portfolio Match** 🟢 Strong Match · 🟡 Partial Match · ⚪ No Match
🧪 **Test** 💵 Paid Test · ⚪ No Test · ❓ Unknown
🤖 **Scout** 👤 Ahmed · 🤖 Jerry · ♊ Gemini · 🟣 Claude · 💻 Codex
📝 **Listing Detail** 🟢 Detailed · 🟡 Adequate · 🔴 Sparse · ⚪ Unknown. This is a client-quality signal: vague listings raise uncertainty because scope, expectations, and professionalism are harder to judge.
## 🔎 Search brief & AI-team rules {toggle="true"} ## 🔎 Search brief — source of truth for Jerry / Gemini / Claude {toggle="true"} **Search widely; decide selectively.** Public search discovers and filters. Ahmed's logged-in Upwork view verifies private/account-specific details before Connects are spent. **Candidate background** - 6 months of Amazon customer-service experience across email, chat and phone. - Real experience with order status/tracking, delivery delays, refunds, returns, policy explanations, upset customers, basic order changes and escalation. - Strong written English; Arabic native; German basic. - Published simulated e-commerce support portfolio covering WISMO/delayed order, late return and damaged-product escalation. - Zero Upwork earnings/reviews so far; no fake experience or implied tool mastery. **Primary search lane** - Customer Support / Customer Service / E-commerce Support. - Email and chat preferred. - WISMO, shipping, tracking, refunds, returns, replacements, order changes, complaints, retention, chargebacks, internal notes, SOP judgment and escalation are especially relevant. - Marketplace support, SaaS support, customer success/onboarding and adjacent client-service roles may be included when the transferable support core is meaningful. **Market-research lane** - Do **not** restrict discovery only to jobs Ahmed can apply to today. - Preserve useful Conditional / Poor Fit examples when they reveal recurring tools, higher-paying skill ladders, adjacent roles, client expectations or bad tradeoffs. - Poor Fit means **poor current fit for Ahmed**, not necessarily a bad job. **Client-quality preference** - Prefer detailed listings with enough scope to understand what is actually being bought. - Prefer clients with meaningful spend, hires, active contracts, hours and/or review history that show they actually hire. - A sparse listing is a risk signal, especially with a high Connect cost or weak client history. - A serious client can still offer a bad opportunity; client credibility does not erase low pay, unclear scope, excessive hours or a major mismatch. **Competition and freshness** - Proposal count is a signal, **not a gate**. 50+ proposals can remain viable if fit, client quality, economics and activity are strong. - Client activity matters: recent views, interviews, hires and whether hiring already appears advanced. - **Freshness is evidence status, not a rewrite of Fit.** Recent signal / Recheck needed can remain in live pre-application views; Stale evidence / Inactive \>14d / Retired-historical move out of the working Fit Map while staying in the Registry. - **Stale evidence ≠ proven inactivity.** Use `💤 Inactive >14d` only when a dated source actually reports that interval. - Fresh listings are preferred, but older opportunities can remain viable when genuinely current evidence shows continued activity. **Tools and experience gaps** - Shopify, Gorgias, Zendesk, Intercom, Help Scout, Freshdesk and similar tools are acceptable when preferred, adjacent or realistically learnable. - Deep mandatory hands-on expertise is a meaningful gap and should lower Fit / Priority rather than be ignored. - Just-in-time learning is preferred over delaying applications for broad tool study. **Economics** - Normal target: roughly **\$10–\$12/hr**. - Tactical first-review territory: roughly **\$8–\$10/hr** when client/scope/learning value justify it. - \$5–\$7/hr is only worth considering when unusually safe, bounded or strategically useful. - Fixed-price work needs clear scope; headline budget alone is not evidence of good economics. **Schedule** - Time compatibility is a first-class decision factor. - Never infer a required shift from the client's city alone. - Translate only explicitly stated timezones / hours into Cairo time. - Recurring overnight work is a material health/lifestyle cost and needs unusually strong justification. **Tests / safety / proposal behavior** - A small paid trial is positive. - A substantial unpaid trial is unacceptable. - No fake experience, fake metrics or pretending simulations are real client tickets. - Positive conversation is not a hire until a formal Upwork contract exists. - No unfunded fixed-price work. - Proposal #1 paid the setup tax: reuse the workflow instead of rebuilding a seven-hour prototype. **Scout output standard** For each serious public candidate capture: direct Upwork URL, age/activity, pay, hours/duration, channels, tools, schedule/timezone, client spend/hires/hours/reviews when visible, proposals/interviews/hires, strongest fit reason, biggest risk, unmet requirement, and what Ahmed must verify privately. **AI-team rule** Jerry, Gemini and Claude may disagree, but they contribute evidence to the **same Opportunity & Proposal Registry**. They do not create parallel freelancing strategies. Ahmed makes the final application and spending decision. ## 🤝 Shared AI-team rule Ahmed, Jerry, Gemini, Claude and Codex contribute to the **same Registry**. Different scouts can disagree; the row stores the evidence and Ahmed remains the final decision-maker. > **One shared market surface. One decision history. One proposal pipeline.**

	- Local file/document classifier.
	- Local agent with web search through an approved tool.
	- Hybrid workflow that escalates only difficult synthesis to Codex/frontier AI.

	For every experiment, preserve:

	- result quality;
	- failure mode;

Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3d2bd7ade63b818f9b81ec3076427097 as of 2026-10-11T01:23:44.667Z: {"title":"🧭 Projects & Ideas Control Center"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🧭"} Projects & Ideas Registry Physical Whiteboard Operating System — Grammar, Workflow & Design Principles **What this system is for:** keep every worthwhile project, idea, research thread, learning goal, and unfinished piece of work safely recorded — without forcing all of them to compete for attention at the same time. ## 🚦 Start here — the system in 60 seconds ### 1. Capture When something matters enough that you do not want to forget it, add it to the Registry. **Capturing it does not mean committing to it.** ### 2. Classify Give it a **Status**, **Priority**, and realistic **Load** rating. This turns a vague mental obligation into visible information. ### 3. Focus Use filtered views to show only what matters for the question you are asking. The system becomes powerful because it lets you **safely hide** everything else. **Core principle:** the Registry is a memory system, not a giant to-do list. A project can remain valuable for years without being Active today. ## 🧠 Three layers — each has one job
Layer Question it answers What belongs there
⬜ **Physical whiteboard** What deserves my attention *now*? Immediate work, current priorities, daily/weekly focus.
🗂️ **Projects & Ideas Registry** What exists in my world? Active, supporting, waiting, paused, parked, completed, archived, ideas, learning, and research.
📚 **Dedicated project homes** What do we actually know about this project? Mother Threads, documentation, roadmaps, research notes, repositories, local folders, detailed Notion pages, and source material.
## 🎯 Read these four fields first ### 🔥 Priority How important is this in the larger life/project picture? **Critical → High → Medium → Low → Someday** ### 🚦 Status Is this actually moving now, supporting something else, blocked, deliberately paused, or simply preserved? ### 🧠 Cognitive Load How much concentration, learning, judgment, or difficult thinking does *the human* need to provide? ### ➡️ Next Action If this is moving, what is the next concrete step? This may become stale and should be updated when the project changes. > **Priority and Status are different.** Something may be Critical but Waiting, High but Supporting, or Medium but Active. Importance does not automatically mean “work on this continuously.” ## 🏷️ Classification dictionary — what every tag means **The three classification fields answer three different questions:** **Type = What is this?** · **Domain = What area of life/work does it belong to?** · **Role = What function does it serve?** Type is usually one primary label. Domain and Role can legitimately have more than one label. ### Quick example A project called **“Dental Treatment Follow-Up”** can be: - **Type:** Project — because it has a concrete outcome: resume and complete treatment. - **Domain:** Medical + Personal — because it concerns direct healthcare and your own life. - **Role:** Wellbeing + Maintenance — because it protects health and completes overdue care. - **Status:** Active — because it should move now. - **Priority:** Critical — because delaying it carries meaningful downside. - **Load:** whatever *you* experience it as; the load fields are subjective rather than objective. ## 📦 Type — *What kind of thing is this?* {toggle="true"}
Type Use it when… Typical example
📌 **Project** There is a concrete outcome, deliverable, or state you are trying to reach. It may be short or long, but it can meaningfully advance or finish. Build an app, complete dental treatment, renovate a profile.
🔎 **Research** The main activity is investigating a question, subject, decision, or body of evidence. The value is understanding rather than producing a conventional deliverable. Migration research, medical case research, technology deep dive.
🎓 **Learning** The main outcome is increasing your own knowledge or skill through study, practice, coursework, or structured learning. German study, Excel learning, a course.
⚙️ **System** You are building or maintaining repeatable infrastructure, a workflow, database, methodology, or operating structure that supports other work over time. PFS, Project Bootstrap, a planning system.
🗃️ **Resource Archive** The primary job is preserving, cataloguing, organizing, indexing, or making material retrievable rather than studying all of it immediately. Livestream archive, German-post archive.
💡 **Idea** You want to preserve a possibility without committing to execute it. An Idea can later be promoted into another Type if it becomes real work. News bot, article concept, future tool experiment.
## 🗺️ Domain — *What area does it belong to?* {toggle="true"} Domain is **multi-select**. Use the smallest set that genuinely helps you filter the portfolio; do not tag every remotely related area.
Domain Use it for…
💼 **Freelancing** Client acquisition, Upwork, customer support positioning, paid freelance work, portfolio/job-market preparation.
🤖 **AI / Software** Programming, automation, AI tools, local AI, software products, technical systems, experimentation.
💰 **Finance** Spending, budgeting, financial records, savings, financial planning, purchase prioritization.
🎓 **Education** Courses, language learning, deliberate study, skill development, educational resources.
✍️ **Writing** Articles, essays, scripts, content creation, publishing, writing portfolios.
👤 **Personal** Your own life administration, home, relationships, life planning, hobbies, or projects that are primarily personal rather than occupational.
🔬 **Research** Cross-cutting investigative work where research itself is a major component. This can coexist with another domain such as Medical, Personal, or AI / Software.
🫶 **Health / Support** Health-adjacent support, caregiving, wellbeing support, or health-related work centered on helping someone else or managing a broader support context rather than your own concrete treatment episode.
👥 **Community** Work tied to a group, learning community, shared resource, community contribution, or collaborative environment.
🩺 **Medical** Your own concrete healthcare: doctors, dentists, treatment, procedures, tests, appointments, follow-ups, and active care. Use this when the project is directly about receiving or completing medical care.
> **Medical vs Health / Support:** use **Medical** for your own direct care and treatment. Use **Health / Support** for broader support/caregiving contexts or health-related work centered on helping another person. A project can use both only when both meanings genuinely apply. ## 🧭 Role — *Why does this matter / what function does it serve?* {toggle="true"} Role is also **multi-select**. It describes the project's function in your larger life/project ecosystem, not its subject matter.
Role Meaning
💵 **Income** Directly contributes to earning money, getting clients, getting hired, or protecting an income-producing path.
🧱 **Foundation** Builds a base capability, structure, knowledge layer, or prerequisite that enables more important work later.
🧪 **R&D** Exploratory or experimental work where learning, testing feasibility, or discovering possibilities is part of the point.
🔧 **Maintenance** Keeps an existing system, responsibility, health need, workflow, or asset functioning correctly rather than creating something fundamentally new.
📚 **Reference** Mainly worth preserving so it can be consulted later. It may be important without requiring ongoing work.
✨ **Curiosity** Worthwhile primarily because it is intellectually interesting, enjoyable, or personally intriguing — not because it currently supports a critical obligation.
❤️ **Wellbeing** Protects or improves health, energy, quality of life, emotional wellbeing, or sustainable functioning.
## 🔥 Priority — *How important is it in the larger picture?* {toggle="true"}
Priority Meaning
🚨 **Critical** High consequence or time-sensitive enough that it deserves deliberate attention soon. Neglect creates meaningful downside.
⬆️ **High** Clearly important and should remain visible, but it can coexist behind Critical work.
➖ **Medium** Worth doing or preserving, but delaying it is acceptable while stronger priorities exist.
⬇️ **Low** Optional, low-consequence, or easily deferred.
🌱 **Someday** Preserve the possibility; there is no present expectation that it should receive attention.
> Priority describes **importance/consequence**, not effort, difficulty, or whether the project is currently actionable. ## 🚦 Status — *What relationship does it have to attention right now?* {toggle="true"}
Status Meaning
🟢 **Active** Deliberately being advanced now.
🔵 **Supporting** Helps an Active priority but does not deserve its own top-level attention slot.
🟡 **Waiting** Blocked by an external response, event, person, dependency, or timing condition.
🟠 **Paused** Intentionally stopped for now, with a plausible return.
⚪ **Parked** Worth preserving, but there is no current commitment to resume it.
🟣 **Completed** Finished; retained because the result, history, or lessons still matter.
🟤 **Archived** Preserved mainly as history/reference and normally hidden from operational views.
## ⚖️ Load & leverage — *What does this cost the human, and how delegable is it?* {toggle="true"} Project load is **subjective**. It describes the cost to *you*, not an objective technical score.
Field Question to ask Scale
🧠 **Cognitive Load** How much concentration, learning, judgment, decision-making, or difficult thinking does this require from me? Light · Moderate · Heavy · Very Heavy · Unknown
❤️ **Emotional Load** How stressful, anxiety-inducing, emotionally difficult, uncertain, or personally intense is this for me? Light · Moderate · Heavy · Very Heavy · Unknown
👤 **Human Attention** How much direct hands-on involvement does this currently demand from me? Low · Medium · High · Very High · Unknown
🤖 **AI Leverage** How much meaningful execution can realistically be delegated to AI, Codex, automation, or tools? Very High · High · Medium · Low · None · Unknown
**Why this matters:** two projects can consume the same amount of time while feeling completely different. **Very High AI Leverage** means AI/Codex can perform nearly all substantive execution while the human mainly directs, reviews, approves, or contributes product judgment. A long archival task may be Light + High AI Leverage, while a short client proposal may be Heavy + Very High Human Attention. ## 🧱 Documentation — *How recoverable is the project state?* {toggle="true"}
Documentation Meaning
🟢 **Current** Modern documentation exists and accurately reflects the project.
🟡 **Partial** Useful documentation exists, but important context or state is still missing.
🟠 **Needs Backfill** Valuable older work predates the current documentation system; reconstruct it before serious reactivation.
🔴 **None** No meaningful project documentation yet.
🟣 **Complete** The work is finished and the documentation is sufficient for future reference.
**Classification test:** if you can explain a project's **Type, Domain, Role, Status, Priority, and Load** in plain language, the tags are probably serving you. If a tag cannot be justified, remove it rather than keeping it “just in case.” ## 👀 How to use the views - 🗺️ **Portfolio by Status** — best high-level visual overview of where everything sits. - 🔥 **Active Now** — only projects deliberately moving now. - 🧩 **Supporting** — useful work that helps current priorities without becoming another top-level commitment. - 🧠 **Ideas Inbox** — preserve ideas without turning them into obligations. - ⏸️ **Paused & Parked** — things intentionally outside the present attention window. - 🧱 **Documentation Backlog** — older work that should be reconstructed before reactivation. - 📚 **Learning & Research** — isolate educational/research work from execution projects. - ✅ **Completed & Archived** — history and reference without cluttering daily decisions. - 🥧 **Current Cognitive Load** — one-chart Free-plan snapshot of the mental weight of currently relevant work. ## 🔄 A simple operating rhythm 1. **Capture first.** If an idea matters, record it before your mind has to keep carrying it. 2. **Classify honestly.** Status should describe reality, not aspiration. 3. **Keep Active small.** Supporting work can exist without becoming another main project. 4. **Update Next Action when state changes.** Do not maintain it for projects that are safely Parked. 5. **Hide aggressively.** Parked, Completed, and Archived work is safer *because* it is recorded — you do not need to keep looking at it. 6. **Promote deliberately.** Before moving something to Active, ask what it displaces. 7. **Let the whiteboard stay selective.** Notion remembers the portfolio; the wall chooses the present. **The system is succeeding when you can hide something without anxiety because you know it has not been lost.**

source.text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3d7bd7ade63b81f49de0faa2047cb793 as of 2026-10-05T15:30:27.376Z: {"title":"Reading & Knowledge Control Center"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"📚"} **What this system is for:** keep books, articles, AI knowledge threads, Notion guides, papers, reports, and other substantial things worth reading safely tracked — without turning the Projects & Ideas Registry into a reading backlog. **Registry:** Reading & Knowledge Registry — this is the single source of truth. The views below are different windows into the same entries, not separate lists. ## 🚦 Start here — the system in 60 seconds ### 1. Capture When something is worth reading, add it to the Reading Registry before relying on memory. **Capturing it does not mean reading it now.** ### 2. Classify Give it a **Status**, **Priority**, **Reading Mode**, and realistic **Cognitive / Emotional Load**. This turns an invisible reading obligation into visible information. ### 3. Resume When you stop, update **Resume From** and **Last Touched**. The next session should begin from a location, not from the question: “Where the hell was I?” **Core principle:** the Registry is a reading-memory system, not a guilt list. Something can remain valuable in the Queue for months, be Paused deliberately, be Archived without rejection, or be Dropped intentionally when it truly is no longer worth continuing. ## 🧭 Why this exists separately from Projects & Ideas The Projects & Ideas Registry answers **what work, research, systems, ideas, and responsibilities exist**. The Reading & Knowledge Registry answers a different question: > **What knowledge object do I want to consume, where am I in it, how demanding is it, and what should I read next?** A deep ChatGPT thread about USB Power Delivery, a physical novel, a long AI article, and a Notion knowledge guide may all deserve tracking — but they should not become four fake “projects.” Keeping the systems separate prevents the project portfolio from becoming noisy while giving reading its own proper memory. ## 🎯 Read these five fields first ### 🚦 Status What relationship do I currently have with this reading item? ### 🔥 Priority How valuable or time-sensitive is reading this compared with the rest of the queue? ### 🧠 Load How much concentration or emotional capacity will this realistically cost me? ### 📍 Resume From Where exactly should I continue? ### ➡️ Next Reading Step What is the smallest concrete continuation? > **Status, Priority, and Load are different.** A Heavy book can be Low priority. A short article can be Critical. A High-priority thread can be Paused because your current capacity is low. ## 🏷️ Classification dictionary — what every field means **The main classification questions are:** **Type = What kind of knowledge object is this?** · **Format = Where/how am I consuming it?** · **Topic = What is it about?** · **Reading Mode = How deeply do I intend to engage with it?** ## 📦 Type — *What kind of thing is this?* {toggle="true"}
Type Use it when…
📖 **Book** A conventional book, whether physical or digital.
📰 **Article** A standalone article, essay, long-form post, or journalistic piece.
💬 **ChatGPT Thread** A substantial ChatGPT conversation whose value is in reading and understanding the knowledge already produced.
🧾 **Notion / Note** A substantial Notion page, internal guide, structured note, or knowledge document.
📄 **Paper / Report** A research paper, technical report, whitepaper, PDF report, or formal analysis.
🎧 **Transcript / Lecture** A transcript, lecture text, workshop transcript, or spoken-learning material being consumed primarily as knowledge.
## 🚦 Status — *Where is my relationship with it now?* {toggle="true"}
Status Meaning
🔖 **Queue** Captured and worth reading, but not started yet.
📖 **Active** Currently being read or deliberately advanced now. This is the reading-system equivalent of an Active project.
⏸ **Paused** Intentionally stopped for now with a plausible return.
💤 **Stalled** Unintentionally drifted away from, forgotten, or repeatedly avoided despite an intention to continue.
✅ **Completed** Read to the intended stopping point.
📚 **Reference** Kept mainly for lookup or selective rereading; sequential completion may not matter.
🗄 **Archived** Preserved and intentionally moved out of the operational reading flow. There is no present expectation to resume, but the item is not being rejected as useless, boring, or unworthy.
🚫 **Dropped** Deliberately abandoned because it is no longer worth the reading time, has become irrelevant, or you consciously do not want to continue it.
> **Paused vs Stalled vs Archived vs Dropped:** Paused means “not now, but there is a plausible return.” Stalled means the return was intended but the item drifted away. Archived means “preserve this, but remove it from the operational reading flow without making a negative judgment.” Dropped is the deliberate terminal judgment that the item is no longer worth continuing. ## 🔥 Priority — *How much does reading this matter?* {toggle="true"}
Priority Meaning
🚨 **Critical** Time-sensitive or consequential enough that reading it soon matters materially.
⬆️ **High** Clearly valuable and should remain near the front of the reading queue.
➖ **Medium** Worth reading, but delaying it is acceptable.
⬇️ **Low** Useful or enjoyable, but easily deferred.
🌱 **Someday** Preserve the possibility; there is no current expectation to read it.
## 🎯 Reading Mode — *What kind of engagement am I actually asking from myself?* {toggle="true"}
Mode Meaning
🧠 **Deep Study** Slow, deliberate reading where understanding, questioning, notes, or re-reading may matter.
📖 **Normal Read** Read carefully enough to follow and understand without turning it into a formal study project.
⚡ **Skim / Extract** Read selectively to pull out the useful parts rather than consuming every line.
🌿 **Leisure** Reading primarily for enjoyment, rest, narrative, or personal experience.
📚 **Reference Only** No expectation of sequential reading; consult the relevant sections when needed.
**Why Reading Mode matters:** not every saved knowledge object deserves deep study. Sometimes “skim and extract what matters” is the correct completion criterion. ## 💻 Format — *Where/how am I consuming it?* {toggle="true"}
Format Examples
📕 **Physical** Printed book, booklet, printed paper.
📱 **E-book** EPUB, Kindle, Apple Books, other digital book.
📄 **PDF** PDF book, paper, report, guide.
🌐 **Web** Website, online article, documentation page.
💬 **ChatGPT / AI** Knowledge conversation living inside an AI chat.
🧾 **Notion** Notion page or database-backed knowledge document.
📝 **Other Digital** Markdown, Docs, text files, or another digital format.
## 🗺️ Topic — *What is this about?* {toggle="true"} Topic is **multi-select**. Use only categories that genuinely help you retrieve or choose reading later.
Topic Typical material
🤖 **AI / Tech** AI systems, hardware, software, programming, electronics, standards such as USB PD.
💼 **Work / Freelancing** Freelancing, client work, professional skills, customer support, job-market knowledge.
💰 **Finance** Personal finance, economics, purchasing, planning, financial systems.
🎓 **Learning / Education** Study methods, education, courses, structured learning resources.
🧠 **Psychology / Self** Behavior, cognition, relationships, self-understanding, personal development.
🌍 **Science / Society** Science, history, society, public affairs, broad explanatory nonfiction.
📚 **Literature / Fiction** Novels, stories, literary works, narrative reading.
🕌 **Religion / Spirituality** Religious texts, theology, spirituality, Quran-related reading.
🩺 **Health / Medicine** Medical or health-related knowledge material.
🗣️ **Language** German, English, linguistics, language-learning material.
## ⚖️ Load — *What will this cost me to read?* {toggle="true"} The load ratings are **subjective**. They describe Ahmed's actual experience, not how difficult the material is supposed to be for an average reader.
Field Question Scale
🧠 **Cognitive Load** How much concentration, working memory, conceptual effort, or careful reasoning will this require from me? Light · Moderate · Heavy · Very Heavy · Unknown
❤️ **Emotional Load** How emotionally taxing, stressful, intense, personally sensitive, or draining will this material be for me? Light · Moderate · Heavy · Very Heavy · Unknown
> A book can be **cognitively Light but emotionally Heavy**, or technically sophisticated but cognitively Moderate because the subject is familiar. These fields should describe lived reading cost, not prestige or difficulty. ## 📍 Resume From — the anti-reconstruction field {toggle="true"} This is one of the most important properties in the entire system. When stopping a reading item, write the smallest location cue that future-you needs to continue immediately. Examples: - Book → `Page 146 — Chapter 7, after the train scene` - Article → `Section: PPS vs fixed PDOs` - ChatGPT Thread → `Curiosity Corner → USB Power Delivery → continue after Jerry's explanation of USB-PD negotiation` - Notion → `Heading: Database Views — stopped before filters` - Paper → `Page 11 — Results section` **Do not rely on memory when a 10-second update can eliminate a future 20-minute reconstruction.** ## 📊 Progress — useful, but intentionally optional {toggle="true"} **Progress %** is available when a rough percentage helps. It should not become fake precision. For a 300-page book, 45% may be useful. For a branching AI thread or reference document, **Resume From** may be much more meaningful than a percentage. ## 🧾 Why Read + Notes / Takeaway {toggle="true"} **Why Read** answers why this item deserves to exist in the Registry at all. Useful examples: - “Understand USB PD well enough to choose chargers safely.” - “Read for enjoyment and restart fiction habit.” - “Understand this Notion architecture before editing the system.” **Notes / Takeaway** is deliberately lightweight. The Reading Registry is not meant to duplicate a full knowledge-management system. If an item produces extensive notes, those can live in its real home and be linked through **Source / Link**. ## 👀 View guide — ask a question, then choose the view
View Question it answers
📚 **All Reading** What exists in the reading system overall?
🗺 **Reading Pipeline** How is the reading portfolio distributed across Queue, Active, Paused, Stalled, Completed, Reference, Archived, and Dropped?
📖 **Active Reading** What am I deliberately reading at the moment, and where do I resume?
🔖 **Queue / Up Next** What have I captured but not started, ordered by priority?
📍 **Resume Here** Which started items can I continue, and exactly where did I stop?
💤 **Paused & Stalled** What did I stop intentionally versus what simply drifted away?
🌿 **Light Reads** What can I realistically read when concentration is limited?
🧱 **Heavy Reads** Which worthwhile items need deliberate mental capacity?
📚 **Books** What is the state of my physical and digital book reading?
💬 **AI & Knowledge Threads** Which substantial AI conversations and Notion knowledge pages are waiting to be read or resumed?
📰 **Articles & Papers** What shorter/formal written knowledge sources are in the system?
✅ **Completed & Reference** What have I finished or retained primarily for lookup?
🗄 **Archived** What have I intentionally moved out of the operational reading flow while still preserving it for history or a possible distant return?
> The views are meant to **reduce search cost**, not create more obligations. If two views stop answering meaningfully different questions, simplify them. ## 🔄 Operating rhythm ### When capturing something new 1. Add the title. 2. Set **Type** and **Format**. 3. Choose **Status = Queue** unless you are genuinely beginning now. 4. Set Priority and load only as accurately as you currently can. 5. Add the source link or physical-book note if useful. ### When you actually start 1. Change Status → **Active**. 2. Set Reading Mode. 3. Add Started date if useful. 4. Do not activate ten items just because you are interested in them. ### When you stop mid-way 1. Update **Resume From**. 2. Update **Last Touched**. 3. If stopping intentionally, use **Paused**. 4. If you later realize it simply disappeared from your life despite intending to continue, use **Stalled**. ### When finishing Choose the ending that matches reality: - **Completed** → read to the intended end. - **Reference** → valuable for lookup; sequential completion is no longer the goal. - **Archived** → preserve it, but move it out of the operational reading flow without declaring it bad or worthless. - **Dropped** → consciously not worth more reading time or no longer relevant enough to continue. **Preservation rule:** the system should reduce the mental burden of remembering what to read. It should not create a second job called “maintaining the reading database.” Use the minimum metadata that makes re-entry and choice easier. ## 🧭 Decision rules for future Jerry / Codex Before adding complexity, ask: 1. Does this property help Ahmed **choose**, **resume**, or **remember** reading? 2. Is the same information already obvious from another field? 3. Will this make capture slower enough that Ahmed stops using the system? 4. Does the new view answer a different question, or merely show the same list another way? 5. Is this item really reading/knowledge consumption, or is it actually a Project/Research item that belongs in the Projects & Ideas Registry? > **The goal is not to maximize the number of things read. The goal is to make worthwhile reading recoverable, selectable by capacity, and easy to resume.** Reading & Knowledge Registry

<callout icon="🧭" color="blue_bg">
	**Use this page only when you need the method.** The Workbench landing page should stay lightweight; live drafting happens inside each proposal room.
</callout>
## Core architecture
- **Registry:** opportunity facts, Fit, Priority, Stage, Connects, submitted terms, outcomes and durable market evidence.
- **Proposal Drafting Workbench:** navigation into active proposal rooms.
- **Proposal room:** the actual co-working space for one application.
- **Client Brief & Requirements:** reference material you may keep open in another tab.
- **Draft & Refinement:** Ahmed writes; Jerry edits/refines; application questions are worked through here in the same sequence.
- **Proposal Build:** the current paste-ready assembled version only.
- **Optional proof pages:** Loom, test, case exercise, etc. only when the application actually benefits from them.
- **Final QA:** compact pre-submission check.
## Practical rule
> **Do not make Ahmed scroll through methodology before he can write.**
The page that contains Ahmed's draft must open directly onto the writing area. Reference material belongs in neighboring tabs/pages.
## Default proposal workflow
1. Open the proposal room.
2. Open **Client Brief & Requirements** in a second tab if needed.
3. Open **Draft & Refinement** and start writing immediately.
4. Work section-by-section:
	- Ahmed raw text
	- Jerry refinement
	- Ahmed edits / accepts / rewrites
	- move settled material into **Proposal Build**
5. If the job has screening questions, tests, or required answers, work through them inside the same Draft & Refinement page unless a large standalone test genuinely deserves its own page.
6. If a Loom or other extra proof is useful, use its dedicated optional page.
7. Open **Final QA** beside the final build before submitting.
8. After submission, update the Registry. Do not duplicate Registry economics, Stage logic, client-risk analysis, or Connect accounting across drafting pages.
## When to create extra pages
Create a dedicated extra page only when it reduces friction:
- large customer-support test,
- written case exercise,
- long screening questionnaire,
- Loom/video script,
- client-requested plan or audit.
Do **not** create pages just because a category exists in the methodology.
## Writing principle
Ahmed's first draft can be rough. The point of the workspace is to preserve his actual voice and reasoning.
Jerry's role is to:
- identify missing requirements,
- improve structure and clarity,
- remove generic filler,
- challenge overpromising,
- preserve truthful gaps,
- keep the wording recognizably Ahmed's.
## Version-control principle
Do not stack endless Draft 1 / Draft 2 / Draft 3 sections.
- Raw thinking stays in **Draft & Refinement**.
- The best current assembled version lives in **Proposal Build**.
- Replace/improve the current build as we iterate.
- Preserve older versions only when there is a real reason to compare them.
## Registry boundary
Do not copy these into proposal pages unless they directly affect wording:
- full client statistics,
- Connect calculations,
- Fit / Priority reasoning,
- general schedule analysis,
- client-risk analysis,
- after-submission outcome tracking.
Those already belong in the Registry.
## Efficiency
Proposal #1 established the workflow at high setup cost. Future proposals should use the system instead of rebuilding the system.
**Target:** usually 2–3 hours; stay under 5 hours unless the opportunity clearly justifies more.
## If Notion ever becomes slower than writing
The system loses its purpose if navigating it becomes harder than drafting.
If a page does not help Ahmed think, write, compare, or submit, move it behind a reference page or remove it from the live workspace.
</content>
</page>
